newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian assembly approves new first premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian assembly approves new first premier.

text.p: Cambodia's National Assembly on Wednesday approved the nomination of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as the country's new first prime minister in place of ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Assembly officials said more than 80 members in the 120-seat house supported the motion. Two-thirds of the assembly, or 80 votes, were needed for the motion to pass.
A total of 86 members of parliament voted in favour of the motion, four voted against, six abstained and there were three spoiled ballots, assembly officials said.
"I would like to declare that from now on His Excellency Ung Huot will be the first prime minister," acting president of the National Assembly Loy Sim Chheang told the parliament.

Members of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party still in the country nominated Ung Huot to succeed the prince as co-premier. Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh on July 6, backed Ung Huot's nomination.

After taking sole power, Hun Sen said he wanted to keep his Cambodia People's Party's coalition with FUNCINPEC in place and that FUNCINPEC should select a new first prime minister. Ranariddh, who left Cambodia just before he was overthrown, has been calling for opposition to Hun Sen from abroad.
